> Hey, I'm happy to take this, as it is something I'd like too. 
> 
> **Proposed approach:**
> 1. Add an "auto" option to the TUI theme mode (alongside "dark" / "light")
> 2. When set to "auto", detect OS appearance and listen for changes:
> - macOS: Use defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle or the `dark-mode-listener` npm package
> - Linux: Check $XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP + gsettings or similar
> - Windows: Registry check for AppsUseLightTheme
> 3. Store the user's preference (auto/dark/light) in KV storage
> 4. Update theme reactively when OS appearance changes
>

**edit:** 
maybe do something like this instead? 

**Current:** theme is a single string (e.g., "dracula"). Mode is detected once at startup from terminal background.

**Proposed config schema:**
```jsonc
// Simple (backwards compatible)
{ "theme": "dracula" }
// Advanced (new)
{
  "theme": {
    "light": "github",
    "dark": "dracula", 
    "mode": "auto"  // "auto" | "light" | "dark"
  }
}
```
When mode: "auto", detect OS appearance and switch between light/dark themes automatically.

**Questions:** 
- Should "auto" be the default, or should users opt-in?
- Should this be something added to the config options? alongside separate "dark" and "light" themes? This would also handle #3244
- Any concerns with adding a dependency like dark-mode-listener, or prefer a shell-based approach?

This opencode behaviour is a problem for me too, and I found this bug while looking for how the session titles were constructed.

I want to use opencode in two modes:

- vibe coding things which are 99% public anyway
- editing my personal notes which I want to stay private

In order to do this I have:

- coding models (using various providers, including opencode)
- local models (using locally hosted models, various servers)

When editing my notes I'm expecting slower responses, and this is a tradeoff I've made for privacy. 

How the session titles were generating so fast was suspicious. 

It seems that at the moment, if I have "other providers" than my local models, some parts of the sessions with the local models may leak to those providers.

Is there a way for me to configure opencode that I can meet both my use cases, or do I need to maintain multiple config files?
Correct me if i'm wrong, but isn't this just a symptom of the theme in your actual terminal vs. the theme of your opencode? Edit: Nevermind, I see it now

Thanks for the detailed bug report and excellent analysis @uf-hy! You've correctly identified the root cause.

This is a confirmed bug and is related to #8676 (which covers the Desktop/Tauri case). There's already an open PR #9095 that addresses TUI auth when using HTTP mode, but it **doesn't fix the plugin client path** you've identified in `plugin/index.ts`.

Your analysis is spot-on:
- `worker.ts` correctly uses `getAuthorizationHeader()` to add Basic Auth
- `plugin/index.ts` creates the client without any auth headers

**Next Steps:**
We'll either extend PR #9095 to also fix the plugin client, or create a separate targeted fix. The fix is straightforward - using a similar `fetchWithAuth` wrapper like the TUI worker does.

For now, the workaround is to not set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` when using plugins that make SDK API calls, or use the CLI without the server password when testing plugins.

Linking this to #8676 for tracking. Thanks for the clear reproduction steps!

Heads up - #9706 was just opened which identifies the same auth header issue but specifically for the **plugin client** in `plugin/index.ts`.

This PR fixes the TUI HTTP mode auth, but the plugin client at `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:24-28` also needs the same treatment - it creates a client without auth headers.

Could we extend this PR to also add auth headers to the plugin client fetch wrapper? The fix would be similar to what you've done for the TUI worker.

> I managed to get it to work, in my case
> 
> If you’re running OpenCode on a remote server over SSH, the OAuth callback to http://localhost:1455/auth/callback will fail unless you forward the port to your local machine.
> 
> What worked for me:
> 
> ssh -L 1455:127.0.0.1:1455 user@remote-ip
> This forwards your local `localhost:1455` to the remote server’s `localhost:1455`, where OpenCode is listening for the callback.
> 
> After reconnecting with this tunnel and re-running the auth flow, the login worked
> 
> Hope this helps anyone else running into this

Adding another concrete use case for per-subagent model selection at spawn time.

## Context / real-world driver (GSD model profiles)

I’m working with **gsd-opencode** (an OpenCode adaptation of the “get-shit-done” workflow) and trying to add “model profiles” where different roles use different models (planner vs executor vs verifier), similar to the original Claude Code setup.

- OpenCode adaptation: https://github.com/rokicool/gsd-opencode
- Original Claude Code reference: https://github.com/glittercowboy/get-shit-done

## Why call-time model selection matters

In the Claude Code GSD workflow, the orchestrator reads a project-local config (e.g. `.planning/config.json` with `model_profile: quality|balanced|budget`) and then spawns different subagents with different models *in the same run* (e.g. planning = higher quality, execution = balanced, verification = cheaper).

In OpenCode today, `task` invocations can’t cleanly replicate that pattern because the Task tool schema does not allow specifying a model at call time. The model used by a Task/subagent is effectively:

- the subagent’s statically configured `agent.model`, otherwise
- inherits the caller’s session/message model.

That forces awkward workarounds (duplicate agents pinned to different models, or rewriting agent definitions between runs) instead of a clean orchestrator-driven “profile” switch.

## Minimal request

Add an optional way to choose the subagent model **at Task spawn time** (e.g. `model` as a string like `anthropic/...` or an enum `model_tier`), so orchestrator-style workflows (like gsd-opencode) can select different models per subagent without duplicating agents.

Suggested resolution order:

1) If Task call specifies `model`/`model_tier`, use it.
2) Else if agent has `agent.model`, use it.
3) Else inherit parent session model.

This preserves current behavior by default.

Related to #5092, I see that bash tool output already streams via MessageV2.Event.PartUpdated with accumulated state. I'm requesting the same pattern be applied to tool arguments during the pending phase.

Currently, it looks like the bash output streams incrementally but the tool arguments are only available after full completion. The tool-input-delta events exist but are discarded in processor.ts. Applying the same accumulate-and-emit pattern would give developers early access to fields like path without waiting for the entire tool call to complete, improving UX for consumers who rely on downstream UI built off this.

This feature, once implemented, would be a game-changer for lightweight local models.

At present, local models such as `Phi4` or `gpt-oss` typically fail with errors like:
`the request exceeds the available context size, try increasing it.`

However, after manually reducing the JSON payload by intercepting and modifying the HTTP request (using a web debugging proxy and regex-based stripping), these models work correctly with OpenCode.

Providing a supported way to minimise system prompts and tool instructions would be extremely valuable and would significantly improve the usability of lightweight local models.
